title: AQE Canonical Defect Report
description: Single source of truth for a defect. Organised around a correlation ID so front-end, network and back-end evidence line up on one timeline. Renders to Markdown (human), Jira ADF, and a GitHub issue body without restating facts.

id.description: Tracker key once filed (e.g. PROJ-1234). Absent until the report is filed.

fingerprint.description: Deterministic dedupe hash. Derived ONLY from stable facts: primary component, error class, boundary endpoint+status, suspected layer. Excludes timestamps, trace IDs, user data and counts so the same defect always hashes identically.

title.description: [Component] fails [Condition] causing [Impact] - see bug-reporting-excellence for the formula.

digest.description: Read-first summary. An agent triaging a queue should need only this field. State the layer verdict and the one fact that proves it.

severity.description: Matches the bug-reporting-excellence rubric. critical=system down/data loss/security; high=major feature broken for many users; medium=partial break with workaround; low=cosmetic or rare edge case.

priority.description: Scheduling decision, distinct from severity. A low-severity bug on a demo path can still be P1.

defect_type.description: integration-contract is the FE/BE payload-shape mismatch class; integration-timing covers race conditions, stale reads and out-of-order responses.

reliability.description: How consistently the reproduction steps produce the failure.

reproduction_rate.description: Observed rate when reliability is intermittent, e.g. '3/10 attempts'.

regression_since.description: Build, release or commit SHA where this last worked, when known.

url.description: Page or endpoint where the defect surfaces. Strip query-string credentials and session tokens before recording.

feature_flags.description: Flag name to state. A flag skew between FE and BE is a leading cause of contract drift - record both sides when known.

tenant.description: Tenant or account identifier, if the defect is tenant-specific. Use an internal ID, never a customer name or email.

preconditions.description: State that must hold before step 1 (logged-in role, seeded data, flag state).

steps.description: Human-readable ordered steps. One observable action each.

executable.description: Machine-replayable form of the same steps. Makes the report an executable artifact instead of a description of one.

engine.description: qe-browser steps are valid input to .claude/skills/qe-browser/scripts/batch.js --steps

steps.description: For engine=qe-browser: batch.js step objects ({action, ...}). Replay with: jq -c '.reproduction.executable.steps' report.json | xargs -0 -I{} node .claude/skills/qe-browser/scripts/batch.js --steps {}

verified_replayable.description: True only when these steps were actually executed and reproduced the failure. Never assert without running them.

expected.description: The behaviour the system is specified to produce, and where that specification lives if it is written down.

actual.description: What happens instead, with the verbatim error text. Quote errors exactly - paraphrased stack traces are not searchable.

components.description: Where in the DOM the defect manifests, resolved as far toward source code as the evidence allows. Ordered most-implicated first.

evidence.description: Every observed fact, each with a stable citable ID (EV-01, EV-02, ...) so prose elsewhere in the report and any downstream LLM can reference it without restating it.

timeline.description: Evidence IDs in observed chronological order across all layers. This is what makes a 200-OK-but-broken-UI defect legible: the interleaving is the diagnosis.

boundary.description: The FE/BE integration point under suspicion. Required in practice for defect_type integration-contract or integration-timing.

correlation_id.description: Trace ID tying UI, network and backend evidence together (traceparent, x-request-id, or equivalent). The single most valuable field for cross-layer root causing.

request_headers.description: Diagnostically relevant headers only (content-type, accept, api-version, traceparent). Authorization and Cookie MUST be dropped, not masked.

service.description: Owning backend service, when resolvable from the route or gateway.

contract_delta.description: Payload-shape mismatch expressed as a path-level diff. This is the defect for most FE/BE integration bugs - a 200 response whose body does not match what the client parses.

contract_source.description: Where 'expected' comes from: an OpenAPI path, a TypeScript interface, a Pact contract, a GraphQL schema field.

path.description: JSON pointer or dotted path into the payload, e.g. 'data.order.total'.

expected.description: Expected type or value per the contract source.

actual.description: What the response actually carried. Redact values that are user data - the shape is what matters.

consumer_impact.description: The concrete client-side consequence, e.g. 'OrderSummary.tsx:42 dereferences total, throws TypeError'.

fault_localization.description: The layer verdict, stated as a hypothesis with its supporting evidence and the alternatives considered. An honest 'unknown' with ruled-out alternatives is more useful than a confident guess.

suspected_layer.description: Use 'contract' when neither side is individually wrong but their agreement is - the FE parses what the BE never promised, or the promise changed unannounced.

rationale.description: Why this layer, citing evidence IDs. Must reference at least one EV- id.

alternatives.description: Layers considered and why they were ranked lower. Stops the assignee re-treading ground.

open_questions.description: What could not be determined from available evidence, and what would settle it.

description.description: Who is affected and what they cannot do. Concrete user consequence, not severity restated.

users_affected.description: Scope estimate with its basis, e.g. 'all checkout users on Chrome (~40% of traffic, per analytics)'.

workaround.description: A workaround that exists, or an explicit statement that none was found.

suggested_assignee.description: Derived from git history on the implicated source file. A hint for the triager, never an auto-assignment.

assignee_basis.description: How the suggestion was derived, so a wrong guess is auditable.

duplicate_of.description: Existing tracker key when fingerprint matching found this defect already filed.

linked_tests.description: Test files that should have caught this. A defect with no candidate test is a coverage gap worth naming.

path.description: Local path or tracker attachment URL.

redacted.description: Whether the redaction gate has processed this file. HAR files and server logs MUST be redacted before filing to an external tracker.

generated_by.description: Skill and version that produced this report, e.g. 'defect-report@1.0.0'.

reporter.description: Human or agent that observed the defect.

applied.description: False blocks filing to any external tracker.

filed.description: Populated only after a successful file operation.

component.description: One implicated UI component, resolved from DOM node toward owning source file.

role_in_defect.description: failing = where the error surfaces; trigger = what the user interacted with. These are often different components, and saying which is which saves the assignee a hop.

selector.description: CSS selector locating the node. Prefer a data-testid-anchored selector over a positional one - positional selectors rot.

dom_path.description: Ancestor chain from document root to the node, outermost first.

component.description: Framework component name at this level, when detectable.

framework_component.description: Component name or nesting path, e.g. 'CheckoutPage > OrderSummary'. Detected from framework devtools attributes, data-component, or data-testid.

detection_method.description: How framework_component was determined. 'inferred' signals a guess the reader should verify.

text_content.description: Visible text, truncated. Helps a human find the element on screen.

state_snapshot.description: Observable element state at failure time: disabled, aria-invalid, value, visibility, class flags.

source_file.description: Repo-relative path, optionally with :line. Closes the loop from DOM node to the code that owns it.

source_basis.description: How source_file was resolved (grep for testid, component name match, stack frame). Distinguishes proof from guess.

owner.description: Most frequent recent author of source_file, from git history.

layer.description: Which tier of the stack produced this observation. The distribution across layers is itself a signal.

summary.description: One line stating the observation. Factual, not interpretive - interpretation belongs in fault_localization.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 absolute time. Required for anything that participates in the timeline.

offset_ms.description: Milliseconds from the first evidence item. Cheaper to read than absolute timestamps when correlating layers.

correlation_id.description: Trace ID linking this item across layers. Matching values on a ui item and a backend item are what turn two observations into one finding.

component_ref.description: Component id (C-01) this observation attaches to.

detail.description: Verbatim payload: error text, stack trace, log line, response body excerpt. Redacted before filing.

attachment_ref.description: Path of the attachment carrying the full artifact.
